title: Wallaby 1,000 has 'dream come true' as Australia thrash Japan

By Michael Doyle

Topic:Rugby Union

Massimo De Lutiis (centre) scored on his Wallabies debut. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

Massimo De Lutiis has enjoyed a dream debut for Australia, as the 1,000th Wallaby scored a try in his country's commanding 56-17 win over Japan in the second Test.

De Lutiis came on in the 50th minute of the Test match in Townsville with the match delicately poised at 21-17, the half-time score.

But the introduction of the hulking 22-year-old began the start of Australia's dominance in the Test match, as fellow prop Angus Bell scored the first of five second-half tries.

De Lutiis, with the descendants of the very first Wallaby Patrick Carew in attendance, scored minutes later to send his teammates, and the crowd, into a frenzy.

"One thousand is awesome. But just to be a Wallaby in general is crazy to me. It's a dream come true," De Lutiis told the Nine Network post-match.

"When I scored, I was just over the moon. I couldn't believe it."

After a difficult first half, the Wallabies improved in attack and defence to earn the win. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

Despite the impressive scoreline, the Wallabies were tested in the opening 50 minutes, with the Japanese taking the lead late in the first half.

At three tries apiece after 40 minutes, the Brave Blossoms had every right to believe a maiden win over the Wallabies was there for the taking.

But Australia showed the polish which eluded them in the first half, and the first Test in Osaka last weekend.

New coach Les Kiss, in his second match in charge, provided the right team talk at half-time to wrestle momentum from Japan.

"We got challenged by Les [Kiss] at half-time," captain Harry Wilson told the Nine Network.

"A team like Japan, if you're not up for it, they really make you pay.

"I was really proud of the group in the second half. We stepped it up and put on a great performance."

The win is Australia's third in a row, the first time the Wallabies have strung together a trio of triumphs since 2024.

The challenge for Australia gets harder, with two Tests in Argentina followed by one Test against South Africa, and two Bledisloe Cup matches against the All Blacks.

Relive all the action from the second Test between Australia and Japan in the blog below.

By Michael Doyle

— reporting by AAP

Australia's forward pack have dined out as the Wallabies wriggled out of an awkward spot to streak away from Eddie Jones' Japan in Townsville.

The host's 56-17 triumph was in the balance until midway through the second half, when the 1000th Wallaby, Massimo De Lutiis, subbed on and stormed over for a debut try to create an 18-point lead.

It was one of six tries from Australian front-rowers on Saturday and — after a three-point win in Osaka seven days earlier — was the welcome breathing room coach Les Kiss was searching for in his second game in charge.

Taniela Tupou barged over for two close-range tries in the first half while Angus Bell added one, hooker Josh Nasser opened the scoring and his replacement Brandon Paenga-Amosa finished the job.

Carter Gordon controlled play nicely in his return at flyhalf while halfback Ryan Lonegan (5/5) was perfect off the tee.

Unforced errors kept Japan in it through the first half and the visitors led 17-14 before Tupou snuck in his second try before halftime to trigger a run of 42 consecutive points.

Slowly the hosts turned the screws, Carlo Tizzano pilfering three times and Fraser McReight immediately adding a steal when he came on in the final 15 minutes.

The Reds flanker replaced lock Lachlan Shaw, who held the lineout together in his starting debut, teaming with fellow pilferer Tizzano and shifting Harry Wilson into the second row.

That finally broke the Japanese resistance, with Charlie Cale and Harry Wilson getting on the board before Paenga-Amosa's after-the-buzzer effort.

Isaac Henry was also impressive in his second Test and first start in the No.13, replacing the injured Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to give Kiss food for thought ahead of a two-Test tour of Argentina.

Henry's straight running busted the line regularly, with his assist for Lonergan waved away due to an earlier forward pass.

It was mission accomplished for Kiss, who avoided two banana-peel clashes against the side that dropped from 10 to 12 in the world last week.

And his selections, explained as "future-proofing" were also validated after in-form lock Josh Canham and prop Allan Alaalatoa were both rested in Townsville.

The Test matches get tougher from here, but the Wallabies are now on a three-match winning streak.

Identifying tactical weaknesses that could be addressed , and the Wallabies constantly were slow to move forward in defence, therefore taking the pressure off, allowing the Japanese room that they should never have had.

- martin Doyle

Excellent structure,the backs will have a say in next Test

By Michael Doyle

6 of 8 tries by the front row for the Wallabies... the backs will be out of the business shortly

- Louise

Watching forwards score tries is my idea of perfect reality TV.

More of it I say.

We don't want to see backs scoring.

By Michael Doyle

Massimo De Lutiis became the 1,000th capped Wallaby today.

He also scored a debut try.

Here are some of his comments, speaking with broadcaster Stan Sport.

1,000 is awesome. But just to be a Wallaby in general is crazy to me. It's a dream come true.

When I scored I was just over the moon. I couldn't believe it.

By Michael Doyle

Australia struggled in the first half, despite holding a 21-17 lead at half-time.

Japan was playing with energy and, at times, the Wallabies were struggling to keep up.

Wallabies captain Harry Wilson told Stan Sport the team was challenged at half-time by coach Les Kiss, and they responded well.

We got challenged by Les [Kiss] at half-time.

A team like Japan, if you're not up for it they really make you pay.

I was really proud of the group in the second half. We stepped it up and put on a great performance.

By Michael Doyle

Japan captain Warner Dearns has spoken to host broadcaster Stan Sport.

Japan were really good in the first half, and held a narrow lead late in the opening 40 minutes.

But that was as good as it got. as the Wallabies dominated the second half to run out handy winners.

Here is Dearns and his thoughts:

It was a good, tough, really hard battle. Credit to the Wallabies, they came out and gave us one in the second half, which we couldn't keep up with.

We knew that the Wallabies were going to come out hard. They had a big, physical pack at the start of the first half, so we put a real emphasis on trying to move them around and play a bit of our fast rugby.

I think we did it well in the first half, but we couldn't keep it going in the second half.

By Michael Doyle

Isaac Henry has spoken to host broadcaster Stan Sport following the Wallabies 56-17 win over Japan.

The Wallabies were tested in the first half, where Japan led at one point.

But the Wallabies came out in the second half and were an improved outfit.

Here are some of Henry's thoughts on the win.

I think all the boys worked extreamly hard and I just tried to do my job the best I could.

We weren't happy with some of the possessions we had in the first half and I think we kind of fixed that up a little bit.

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

The Wallabies have produced a brilliant second half to secure a dominant 56-17 win over Japan in the second Test, as Australian rugby history was made.

Massimo De Lutiis became the 1,000th capped Wallaby ever, when the hulking prop came on after 50 minutes in Townsville and made an impact with a try less than 10 minutes later.

The Wallabies were tested in the first half by Japan, who had never beaten Australia in eight previous attempts, as both teams scored three tries in the opening 40 minutes.

But Japan wilted in the second half as the Wallabies piled on five tries.

By Michael Doyle

It is a cherry on top for Australia.

They marched down field, earned a penalty, and just kept hammering the Japanese line.

Ultimately, it was Brandon Paenga-Amosa who crashed over from close range.

Australia 56

Japan 17

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

Japan's replacement hooker Mamoru Harada was sent to the sin bin after that last Wallaby try.

The Wallabies were playing with advantage for the hooker being offside.

Japan was warned earlier about infringements on the goal-line, and Harada has been given an early shower.

By Michael Doyle

The Wallabies are really humming now.

A line break from Tom Wright (15) down the right flank, followed by a pass to Tate McDermott (21) put Japan on the backfoot.

The Wallabies then did what they have done all game when they get inside the Japan 22, they hammer with the forwards.

Pick-and-drives, short passes to big men, the Wallabies hammer and hammer until captain Harry Wilson crashes over.

Australia 49

Japan 17

By Michael Doyle

Fabulous from the Australian forwards.

The Wallabies had a scrum 10 metres out. The Wallabies anhilated the Japan scrum, pushing them back six metres before Charlie Cale, in the number 8 posiiton, picked the ball up and had no-one in front of him.

Great try by the big guys.

Australia 42

Japan 17

By Michael Doyle

The Wallabies are on the attack, and Japan has given away a penalty.

Japan has now been warned for too mamy penalties while defending the goal-line.

The Wallabies attacked the Japanese goal-line, with a chance to end this contest.

But a knock-on close to the line has kept the Japanese in this contest.

Australia 35

Japan 17

By Michael Doyle

Japan's attack in this second half has been nullified by a brilliant display from Australia in the ruck.

Four times the Wallabies have forced a penalty with the Brave Blossoms on the attack, getting their hands on the ball and forcing a penalty.

Carlo Tizzano (7) has been responsible for three of the penalties, in a textbook display of openside flanker play.

Australia 35

Japan 17

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

What a moment.

Wallaby 1,000, Massimo De Lutiis, has scored on debut.

It came off a line break from fly half Carter Gordon, who was brought down close to the line.

Subsitiution lock Jeremy Williams gave a lovely pass from the ruck, and De Lutiis charged onto the ball to score.

There is a party in Townsville.

Australia 35

Japan 17

By Michael Doyle

Both starting props have now scored for the Wallabies.

From close range, Angus Bell crashes over.

The Wallabies have a new game plan: box kick high and let winger Max Jorgensen chase and catch it.

It put them in an attacking positon, and then a penalty allowed the home side to kick for touch and have a line out from close range.

The Wallabies played off the line out, attacked the middle of Japan's defence, and muscled their way over.

Ryan Lonergan converts.

Australia 28

Japan 17

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

History has been made in Townsville.

Hulking prop Massimo De Lutiis has run onto the field for his international Test rugby debut.

The 22-year-old, who plays club rugby for the Queensland Reds, is the 1,000th capped Wallaby.

The Wallabies made two changes here.

ON: Massimo De Lutiis (18); OFF: Taniela Tupou (32)

ON: Jeremy Williams (19); OFF: Lukhan Salakaia-Loto (5)
